name: Radiation Enteritis

prevalence.estimate: 1 in 1,000 patients receiving abdominal or pelvic radiation

criteria.description: History of prior abdominal or pelvic radiation therapy
Presence of chronic gastrointestinal symptoms such as abdominal pain, diarrhea, or malabsorption
Endoscopic evidence of mucosal inflammation, ulceration, or strictures in irradiated bowel segments
Radiologic findings consistent with bowel wall thickening, strictures, or fistulas on CT or MRI
Exclusion of other causes of enteritis such as infection or inflammatory bowel disease

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: History of radiation exposure plus at least two major criteria including clinical symptoms and endoscopic or imaging findings
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is clinical and supported by imaging and endoscopy; biopsy may be used to exclude other etiologies.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Chronic abdominal pain localized to irradiated bowel segments
searchTerms: chronic belly pain in radiation area
ongoing diarrhea with poor nutrient absorption
nausea and vomiting on and off

occasional.symptomName: Bowel obstruction symptoms including cramping and constipation
Fistula formation between bowel and adjacent organs
searchTerms: abnormal connection between bowel and other organs

occasional.symptomName: Fatigue related to chronic disease state

rare.symptomName: Sepsis secondary to bowel perforation or fistula
searchTerms: severe infection from bowel leak or fistula

rare.symptomName: Severe electrolyte imbalances due to malabsorption
searchTerms: serious electrolyte problems from poor absorption
imbalanced body salts due to malabsorption

laboratory: Anemia due to chronic blood loss
imaging: CT scan showing bowel wall thickening and strictures
MRI demonstrating fibrosis and inflammation of bowel segments
Contrast studies revealing strictures or fistulas
other: Endoscopic visualization of mucosal ulceration, telangiectasia, and fibrosis
Histopathology showing chronic inflammation, fibrosis, and vascular changes

distinguishingFeatures: Positive stool cultures or PCR for pathogens

redFlags: Severe abdominal pain with signs of peritonitis
Signs of bowel obstruction or perforation
references: Andreyev HJN. Gastrointestinal complications of pelvic radiotherapy: are they of any importance? Gut. 2005;54(8):1051-1054.

Panes J, Bouhnik Y, Reinisch W, et al. Management of radiation enteritis: a systematic review. J Crohns Colitis. 2020;14(6):741-753.
